correctness.rationale: Free amalgamation identifies all complete nonalgebraic one-point types with link-pair Boolean assignments avoiding an all-three-pair clause for each old triple. Disjoint clauses have probability 1-p^3; two that share an old pair have joint probability 1-2p^3+p^5. Select a maximum matching in the old-triple overlap graph and apply Harris to decreasing block events. For equality, two different blocks sharing an essential Boolean variable have strictly positive covariance via conditioning on it, hence the product lower bound is strictly smaller; no outside-block overlap is equivalent to matching-plus-isolates. Disjoint four-vertex two-triple and three-vertex one-triple blocks attain every (m,nu); first overlap gives 50 rather than 49 types. Independent check enumerated all 785 admissible n=3..5 bases and exact p=1/2 counts, but the Harris proof establishes general n and p.

evidence: General positive association applies to all decreasing events but is not an explicit sharp formula in old-triple matching number with all equality cases. The published K4-minus-free type-polytope theorem concerns an age forbidding three of four triples, not the weaker all-four forbidden age.

value.rationale: The first tight structural correction to the independent-clause 1-type count is a natural invariant of the parameter incidence pattern. Equality and realizability distinguish disjoint overlap motifs from pencils and provide useful quantitative type-space bounds.

final_claim: For finite tetrahedron-free parameter 3-hypergraph A with m old edges, N=binom(n,2), and overlap graph matching number nu, normalized nonalgebraic 1-type polynomial obeys F_A(p)>=(1-p^3)^(m-2nu)(1-2p^3+p^5)^nu for 0<p<1, equality exactly when overlap graph is matching plus isolates; all (m,nu) sharp.
limitations: Only single new-vertex types in tetrahedron-free generic three-uniform hypergraph, no all-base exact polynomial closed form.
